bridge: Builds on F05 dependencies, I01 model lifecycle and G02 data rights.
teaching:
A tokenizer converts input into representation units; an adapter is an additional learned component that can modify a base model’s behaviour; a loader is the code that reads those artifacts into a framework. A corpus is a collection of documents. Each may have its own publisher, version and risks.

AI supply chains include code, model weights, tokenizers, adapters, datasets, prompts, container images and external tools. A checksum establishes equality to a chosen artifact, not that the artifact's publisher or behaviour is trustworthy. Record provenance, revision and license/usage conditions.

Some model formats or loading options can execute code. Do not enable remote code or load an unfamiliar serialized object merely to inspect it. Use supported safer formats and isolation under the selected framework's official guidance. Keep deployment secrets outside training/build contexts and scope model-service credentials.

Poisoning changes data or artifacts so later behaviour is altered. Distinguish a poisoned training set, a malicious fine-tuning adapter and a compromised retrieval document. They enter at different stages and need different provenance and rollback controls. A package vulnerability scanner alone does not assess semantic model behaviour or dataset legitimacy.

The assigned video treats the model as one software-supply-chain component. Keep that distinction: an API endpoint, downloaded weights, a tokenizer, adapter and loader can have different owners and revisions. A model name alone is not a release identifier. A scanner can find selected known code threats, but cannot establish that training data was legitimate, that a semantic backdoor is absent or that the application’s tool permissions are safe. The exercise is a manifest review; no artifact is downloaded or executed.
example:
Synthetic release manifest
code: commitC1
model: publisherP, revisionM1, digestH1
tokenizer: revisionT1
adapter: none
retrieval corpus: versionD1, approved owner/source list
loader: no unreviewed remote-code execution
rollback: known previous manifest
Unknown: behaviour outside tested/task scope
explanation: The manifest exposes missing provenance before running anything. A later adapter addition is a release change even if the base model digest is unchanged. A matching digest does not validate training-data rights or prove absence of a backdoor.
exercise: Review a changed release: same model name but no revision/digest, new adapter from an unknown publisher and a loader asking to execute remote code. Identify distinct risks and decide what evidence is required before an isolated authorised review.
solution: Unpinned version undermines reproducibility; unknown adapter changes behaviour/provenance; remote code adds execution risk. Obtain source/revision/license/security information, inspect configuration and use an approved isolation/review process. Do not download/run the artifact as part of this exercise.
challenge: Write an AI bill-of-materials record for a fictional RAG assistant and a rollback plan after suspected corpus poisoning. Explain how rollback differs for corpus, model and application-code changes.
challenge_solution: Version each component and retain trusted prior releases. Revoke poisoned corpus entries and derived caches/indexes; select a verified prior model/adapter if affected; redeploy reviewed code when its path is compromised. State remaining uncertainty rather than declaring a rollback complete from a filename alone.
